Product.heading: Product and Service Offerings
Product.text: We offer a variety of EV charging products and services to Property Partners and EV drivers.

Service.heading: Product and Service Offerings
Service.text: We offer a variety of EV charging products and services to Property Partners and EV drivers.

Network.text: We are a leading owner, operator, provider, and manufacturer of EV charging equipment and networked EV charging services in the rapidly growing U.S. and international markets for EVs. Blink offers residential and commercial EV charging equipment and services, enabling EV drivers to recharge at various locations. Blink’s principal line of products and services is its Blink Networks and Blink EV charging equipment, also known as electric vehicle supply equipment (“EVSE”), and other EV-related services. The Blink Networks are a proprietary, cloud-based system that operates, maintains, and manages Blink charging stations and handles the associated charging data, back-end operations, and payment processing. The Blink Networks provide Property Partners, among other types of commercial customers, with cloud-based services that enable the remote monitoring and management of EV charging stations. The Blink Networks also provide EV drivers with vital station information, including station location, availability, and fees (as applicable).

Car-Sharing Services.text: Car-sharing services revenues were $1,175 during the three months ended March 31, 2025 as compared to $1,097 during the three months ended March 31, 2024, an increase of $78, or 7%. The increase in revenues is due to the increase in properties and participants subscribing to the car-sharing services.

Warranty.text: Warranty revenues were $955 for the three months ended March 31, 2025 as compared to $953 for the three months ended March 31, 2024, an increase of $2. The increase was primarily attributable to an increase in warranty contracts sold for the three months ended March 31, 2025 as compared to the three months ended March 31, 2024. During the three months ended March 31, 2025, the Company recognized net revenues for the sale of Blink warranty programs to a third party of ($19).

The increase in depreciation expense was attributable to the increase in Company-owned DC Fast chargers that are operational.

nonint.heading: Operating Expenses
nonint.text:
Compensation expense decreased by $4,904 or 42%, to $6,787 (consisting of $6,282 of cash compensation and benefits and $505 of non-cash compensation) for the three months ended September 30, 2026. Compensation expense was $11,691 (consisting of $11,258 of cash compensation and benefits and $433 of non-cash compensation) for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in compensation expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025 was primarily related to decreases in personnel across the Company as a result of cost savings and synergies realized in transformation program.

General and administrative expenses decreased by $2,536 or 68%, to $1,206 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to $3,742 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease was attributable to the general decrease in most expense categories, with legal and professional services contributing to $1,405 of the decrease, due to the transformation initiatives launched during 2025 and realized this year.

Other operating expenses decreased by $2,041, or 42%, to $2,762 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $4,803 for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

nonop.heading: Other Income (Expense)
nonop.text: We recorded other income of $259 during the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to other income of $159 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in other income was primarily related to an increase in dividend and interest income of $107 during the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025, due to higher cash balances compared to prior periods.

net.heading: Net Loss
net.text: Our net loss for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased by $6,369, or 1918%, to $6,701 as compared to $332 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to a gain on settlement related to the Envoy consideration payable recorded during the three months ended September 30, 2025.

da.text: Depreciation and amortization expense increased by $366 or 28%, to $1,684 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to $1,318 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in depreciation expense was attributable to the increase in Company-owned DC Fast chargers that are operational.

wc.text: As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $30,499 compared to $39,568 in cash and cash equivalents as of December 31, 2025, representing a decrease of $9,069 in available liquidity due to ongoing operating losses and working capital requirements.

capex.text: During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net cash used in investing activities was $1,244, of which $1,303 was provided by government grants, $2,122 was used to purchase property and equipment, $250 of cash, net of proceeds received and cash balances transferred to Envoy's buyer, was disposed of in connection with the sale of Envoy, and $175 was used for capitalized engineering costs. During the nine months ended September 30, 2025, net cash provided by investing activities was $11,168, of which $13,630 was provided by the sale of marketable securities, $1,952 was provided by government grants and $223 was provided by the sale of an equity method investment, offset by $207 for the acquisition of Zemetric, net of cash acquired, $205 of capitalized engineering costs and $4,225 of which was used to purchase charging stations and other fixed assets.

net sales.heading: Revenues
net sales.text:
Total revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 decreased by $8,658 or 32%, to $18,397 compared to $27,055 during the three months ended September 30, 2025.

Revenue from product sales was $6,413 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to $13,035 during the three months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of $6,622, or 51%. The decrease was primarily attributable to the Company’s strategic repositioning toward higher-margin market segments and more disciplined customer selection, including a reduction in lower-margin sales. Product revenue was also adversely affected by continued softness in the electric vehicle charging market, particularly lower demand for commercial Level 2 chargers and DC fast chargers, compared to the prior-year period.

Service revenue including charging service revenue from Blink-owned charging stations and network fees was $10,035 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to $10,782 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of $747 or 7%. The decrease is due to the Company exiting lower-margin charging service contracts in Europe.

intro.text: Blink Charging Co. (Nasdaq: BLNK) is a global leader in electric vehicle (EV) charging equipment and services, enabling drivers, hosts, and fleets to easily transition to electric transportation through innovative charging solutions. Blink’s principal line of products and services include Blink’s EV charging networks (“Blink Networks”), EV charging equipment, and EV charging services. Blink Networks use proprietary, cloud-based software that operates, maintains, and tracks the EV charging stations connected to the network and the associated charging data.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
